cohort: The cohort consisted of 821 singleton pregnant women with placental abruption in western Japan (Kyushu-Okinawa Districts) identified from 2005 to 2010.
finding: Exposure to nitrogen dioxide (NO2) at a 2-day lag was associated with placental abruption (temperature adjusted odds ratio per 10 ppb increase = 1.4; 95% confidence interval = 1.1, 1.8).
mod_finding: The association patterns between NO2 exposure and placental abruption were similar when restricted to participants who delivered by emergency cesarean.
cross-section timing: Exposure to air pollutants was assessed at specific lags relative to the day of delivery, with the primary finding related to a 2-day lag.
